transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been having thoughts that scare me. Like… sometimes I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And on the drive home, I’ve found myself wondering if my family or my students would be better off without me. I don’t want to act on it, but the fact that I’m thinking that way really frightened me.
How long have you been having these scary thoughts?
It’s been… about a year and seven months now. It started around when I took over the STEM assessment redesign, on top of my normal teaching load.
Have you noticed any changes in the things you enjoy doing or find pleasurable over the past year and seven months?

Yes. I used to really look forward to things like softball, my book club, working in my garden, and helping with robotics club. Now I either cancel or I show up and just kind of go through the motions. It doesn’t feel enjoyable the way it used to.
Do you still find pleasure in things like eating or sex?

Yeah… in general, things just don’t feel enjoyable anymore. Like I said, I used to look forward to softball, book club, gardening, robotics club, and now I usually cancel or I’m there but just going through the motions. It’s like the pleasure part is kind of gone.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before these thoughts started?

Yes, definitely my energy is lower. By the time I get through teaching and a department meeting, my body feels so heavy. Even making dinner or answering a few parent emails feels like climbing a hill.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than you used to, or do you find yourself fidgeting or restless more often?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed fidgeting more than usual. Maybe I move a little slower when I’m tired, but I haven’t really paid attention to it.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

Yes. I feel guilty a lot. If a lesson doesn’t go well, or a student looks confused, I immediately think it’s my fault and that I’m letting everyone down. I’ll replay it over and over and tell myself I’m a terrible teacher… and then it kind of spills over into feeling like I’m a bad mother too.
Do you think you've been moving more slowly than usual?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower. Maybe when I’m tired I take longer to get going, but I can’t say it’s been a clear change.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are not your own or that someone or something is controlling your mind?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve never felt like someone else was controlling my thoughts or my mind.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past year and seven months?

Yes… I think I have. I don’t really weigh myself much, but my clothes have definitely gotten looser over the past year. I haven’t been trying to lose weight. Most school days I just don’t eat until late afternoon, either I forget or I just avoid it.
Do you feel like you've been restless or having trouble sitting still lately?
Not really. I haven’t noticed myself being restless or unable to sit still. If anything, I just feel kind of worn out, but not like I’m pacing or fidgeting all the time.
How long have you been feeling this low, would you say it's been constant over the past year and seven months or have there been periods where you felt better?

It’s been about a year and seven months now. I think it started around when I took over the STEM assessment redesign on top of my normal teaching load. It hasn’t really felt like I’ve properly gone back to normal since then.
Have you had any periods over the past year and seven months where you felt completely back to normal?

No, not really. There might have been the odd day that was a bit easier, but I don’t think I’ve had a period where I felt completely back to normal. It’s been going on since around when I took on the STEM assessment redesign along with my usual teaching work.
Have you had any days over the past year and seven months where you woke up feeling okay, like your normal self, and the low feelings didn't start until something happened during the day?
I don’t think so. It’s more like it’s just been there most of the time for about a year and seven months, since I took on that STEM assessment redesign on top of my normal teaching workload.
Do you usually wake up feeling low, or does the low feeling develop as the day goes on?
I’m not completely sure. I haven’t really tracked it like that. I think a lot of days I wake up already feeling pretty low, but it can feel heavier as the day goes on too.
Do you usually feel low throughout the entire day, or are there moments during the day when you feel somewhat better?
I’m not really sure. I think it’s there for most of the day, but there might be brief moments where I’m a bit distracted or it feels slightly lighter. I wouldn’t say I feel properly better, though.
Do you usually feel low right when you wake up in the morning?
I think a lot of mornings, yes, I wake up already feeling low. Not every single one that I can clearly remember, but it often feels like it’s there as soon as I’m awake.
Is your low mood usually worse in the morning?
I’m not sure it’s usually worse in the morning. I do often wake up already low, but I can’t really say the morning is the worst part consistently. It varies, I think.
Have you had more than one period of feeling this low in your life, before the past year and seven months?
I’m not really sure. I can’t clearly point to another period before this one that was like this. I’ve had low times, but I don’t know if they were the same or lasted in the same way.
